source_snapshot.procedure: Configure SMTP server/authentication in BMC WebUI, connect, configure alerts and cause an alert; power off/on is offered as an easy example.
source_snapshot.criteria: SMTP server receives the same event information from BMC.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; reads BMC/SEL only and cannot prove server delivery.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION for isolated SMTP, protected secrets, approved event and mailbox correlation.

old_problem: The review method and classification were already sound, but ordinary SMTP endpoint, event and field-mapping inputs kept the case on the decision queue despite source_conflict and blocked both being false.
disposition_reason: The source purpose and oracle are clear: configure the BMC mail client, produce one approved alert, and compare the received message to that event. Server, TLS/authentication, recipient, safe event, delivery deadline and message mapping are Project Configuration. Power off/on is introduced only as an example and is not authorized or required when a safer documented test-alert event provides the same SMTP alert coverage.
decision_basis: XLSX row 830, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2 and historical record were directly reviewed.
RFC 5321 defines SMTP transport; STARTTLS and SMTP AUTH are distinct negotiated extensions whose actual support/policy must be bound to the target BMC and test server.
BMC-side `lan print` or SEL output cannot prove that the server accepted a message or that its content matches the event.
ED-36 makes endpoint/event/timeout values readiness data, while ED power and verdict rules prohibit using the example power transition without separate authorization.

test_case.test_name: Configure secure BMC SMTP alerting and correlate one approved event to the received message
test_case.purpose: Verify the BMC WebUI saves the approved SMTP transport/authentication and recipient configuration, establishes the required protected session, delivers exactly the approved alert to an isolated mailbox, and preserves the same event identity/severity/time/source/message fields end to end.
required_package: Isolated SMTP test server/mailbox, port, hostname, trusted CA/TLS policy and supported AUTH mechanism
Dedicated sender/recipient and protected test credential with no production distribution
Vendor/project-approved non-destructive BMC test alert or bounded event plus expected SEL/event fields
Delivery/duplicate/retry deadline and normalized subject/body/header-to-event mapping
Prior SMTP/recipient state, configuration restore and credential cleanup/revocation plan
test_case.test_command: Back up BMC SMTP/recipient settings and empty or uniquely identify the test mailbox window. Operator configures the actual WebUI with the approved server, TLS, AUTH, sender and recipient using protected secret entry; verify connection without logging credentials. Invoke exactly one approved non-destructive test alert and record its BMC event/SEL ID and timestamp. Collect SMTP server TLS/AUTH/queue/delivery log and raw received message, then compare event ID/source/severity/time/message against the project mapping. Restore settings and remove/revoke temporary recipients/secrets. Do not power-cycle for this review.
test_case.expected_result: The BMC negotiates the required trusted transport/authentication and the isolated server accepts one message for the intended recipient within the approved deadline. The raw message and BMC event have the same normalized event identity, source, severity, timestamp and message content, with no unexpected recipient or duplicate beyond policy. Configuration and secrets return to the approved baseline.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires correlated BMC event evidence plus SMTP server receipt and raw message; BMC logs alone cannot pass. FAIL includes TLS/hostname/auth downgrade or error, absent/late/duplicate delivery outside thresholds, wrong recipient, field mismatch, secret exposure, uncontrolled retry/volume or failed restore. Without an approved event/mapping/deadline execution is NOT READY, not Pending or PASS.
safety_gate: Use only isolated sender/recipient/server; never send to production distribution
Protect BMC/SMTP secrets and require trusted TLS/hostname validation
Use a documented non-destructive alert; no power off/on, power cycle or fault injection under this case
Disable uncontrolled retry and stop on wrong recipient, unexpected volume or auth/TLS failure
Preserve SEL/mail evidence before restoring recipients/settings and revoke temporary credentials
expected_evidence: BMC/firmware identity and redacted WebUI SMTP configuration
SMTP server capability/CA/AUTH policy and secret-handling attestation
Approved stimulus record and exact BMC event/SEL entry
Server TLS/AUTH/session/queue/delivery logs and raw redacted message
Field-by-field event-to-message comparison with delivery/duplicate timing
test_case.recovery: Stop delivery on wrong recipient, secret exposure or uncontrolled retry; disable the test alert destination through the approved UI, restore saved SMTP settings, and revoke/rotate the test credential as needed. Preserve server/BMC evidence and do not resend automatically.

source_conflict.reason: The source consistently targets end-to-end alert delivery; power control is an example stimulus, not required semantics.

blocked.reason: Transport, event and comparison are clear; endpoint/security/stimulus values are readiness inputs.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: SMTP server/TLS/AUTH, sender/recipient, protected credentials, safe event, field mapping, timing and rollback.
